title: Optimizing Network Resilience Using Domain-Specific Hardware Accelerator for Dynamic Programming
problem: Network routing under failures is computationally expensive; GPU/CPU solutions lack specialized hardware
motivation: Dynamic programming kernels in networking; DPA can accelerate recovery and fault tolerance
method: The approach designs a Dynamic Programming Accelerator (DPA)—custom hardware built specifically for dynamic programming, which is a technique where you solve complex problems by breaking them into overlapping subproblems, solving each once, and reusing results instead of recomputing. The hardware is optimized to find optimal network routes when links fail, a computationally expensive problem for general processors. The method shows that this specialized hardware outperforms GPU and CPU solutions on the same task.
key_novelty: Specialized hardware built for dynamic programming finds optimal network routes faster when links fail than general-purpose processors.
contributions: DPA design for dynamic programming operations
